newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Sharon may go to Cairo for gas talks.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Sharon may go to Cairo for gas talks.

text.p: Israel's National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon may go to Cairo next week for talks on energy issues, a ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.
This follows an invitation by Egyptian Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi, which was made through the Egyptian Ambassador to Israel Mohammed Bassiouny.
"The invitation has been received and it is now being considered," the Israeli ministry spokesman said.

The talks are expected to focus on a proposed natural gas pipeline and long-term supply agreement between the two countries. Negotiations between Israel and Egypt resumed last month on natural gas supplies.
The talks have been continuing in recent weeks despite the tension in relations between the two countries following the fighting between Israeli soldiers and Palestinians that killed 74 people.

Israel is interested in purchasing two billion cubic metres of natural gas beginning in the year 2000. The proposed project involves the construction of a pipeline from the gas fields in Egypt's Delta region to the Israeli border and from there through Israel.
